analysis.title: Market Internal Weekly: Three Capitulation Signals vs. Three Systematic Unwinds: Expect a Monday Low
key_insights: UBS US Equity Derivative Strategy says three capitulation signals have triggered: Excess Flow of -$365bn (largest on record), UBS RMM Flow bought the dip at the 68%-tile vs 3Y after the largest selling episode since Covid, and VIX Cross-Asset Rank at 96%. The desk expects SPX could set a low on Monday as systematic selling and hedge-fund unwind pressure fade.

Excess Flow of -$365bn came with SPX -4.4% and QQQ -6.5%. The Sell Flow/SPX ratio of -4.97% is below -4% on only three prior days: 2/5/18 (Volmageddon), 3/12/20 (Covid) and 12/18/24 (FOMC rate cut disappointment). SPX was +1.7%, +9.3% and -0.1% one day later on those dates.
On those three prior days SPX was +0.2%, -2.9% and +2.8% one week later, and +2.7%, +12% and +1.3% one month later.

UBS RMM clients sold heavily until 11:15am (Wednesday post-election plus today's morning), the biggest selling since March 2020. They bought the dip steadily into the close, with net flow at the 68%-tile vs 3Y. The desk still expects more retail selling Friday-to-Monday morning from margin calls.

With VIX at 28.2, VIX Cross-Asset Rank is 96%. A reading above 95% means equity volatility is too high vs other asset classes. Historically (ex Covid) VIX fell 80% of the time over 1M, by an average of 20 points. SPX rose 80% of the time over 1M, by an average of +2.8%.
The VIX/SPX Intraday Hi-Low Ratio test is NOT met. It typically needs SPX below -9.5% from peak, and SPX is only -5.9% from peak.
Three systematic strategies sold an estimated $170-210bn today: Risk Control $95-125bn, Leveraged ETFs $50-55bn and CTAs $25-30bn.

Risk Control funds need an estimated $270-360bn rebalance after SPX -4.4%. About $70-90bn was done today, and $200-270bn remains over the next two days (about $100-135bn a day). After that, RC exposure is 54%, the 21%-tile vs 5Y and the lowest since Apr-Jun 2025, and further selling should have no market impact.
Risk Control daily breakeven is now 1.16%. Next-day scenarios: SPX -3% means about $45bn sold, -2% means $15bn sold, -1% means $5bn bought.

Leveraged ETF selling of $50-55bn was the largest one-day figure on record (SPX -4.4%, QQQ -6.5%). The prior largest was $47bn on Jun 5, 2026 (SPX -2.6%, QQQ -4.8%). The rebalance was concentrated in QQQ and tech at -$46bn: $26bn semis, $15bn QQQ, $1.6bn MAG-7, $4bn other tech.

CTAs sold $25-30bn on 7 sell triggers across ES1, RTY1 and NQ1. Post-rebalance global equity exposure is 3%, the 28%-tile vs 5Y. Only 3 sell triggers remain within -2.5% across ES1 and RTY1, so sell risk is insignificant from here.

CTA trigger detail: ES1 exposure is at the 17%-tile vs 3Y with a close sell trigger at 7348.4 and a medium-term crossover within 4 days. NQ1 exposure is at the 9%-tile with no close sell triggers. RTY1 exposure is at the 16%-tile with a close sell trigger at 2723.4 (-0.4%).

UBS PB L/S positioning is light: gross leverage at the 39%-tile vs 1Y, net leverage at the 14%-tile, and long/short ratio at 1.96x (8%-tile). The desk says net long exposure is very low and short-squeeze risk is high.
No sign of a risk parity unwind today.
Investor conversations were not panicked. Clients recognize more systematic selling is coming and are waiting for entry points to buy the dip.
Dealer gamma as of Nov 4 was long at +$0.98bn (23%-tile vs 5Y). For options expiring from t+1, SPX dealer gamma is bound between -$7bn and +$12bn (at 7830) between 7200 and 8200.

Positioning and flow: total cash is 11.95% of market cap (3%-tile vs 5Y). Russell 2000 short interest is at the 98%-tile vs 5Y. Margin plus leveraged ETF leverage is 2.65% of SPX market cap, 40 bps above the 3Y average. Corporate buyback seasonality is low this week and turns high in the week of Nov 16.

sector_views.rationale: Not a sector call. Leveraged ETF selling was concentrated in QQQ and tech at -$46bn, including $26bn in semis.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Large one-day decline that drove the record Excess Flow and systematic rebalancing.
Nasdaq-heavy selling drove the record leveraged ETF rebalance.
Below the roughly -9.5% typically needed for the VIX/SPX Intraday Hi-Low Ratio signal.
Most of this year's gain came overnight, not in US trading hours.

risk_factors: Further systematic selling: $200-270bn more from Risk Control over the next two days.
Retail margin-call selling expected Friday-to-Monday morning.
Some CTA sell triggers remain, including ES1 at 7348.4 and RTY1 at 2723.4.
The VIX/SPX intraday hi-low ratio test is not met, so capitulation is not confirmed on that measure.
Hedge-fund unwind pressure could continue until Monday.

tension_points.theme: SPX Monday low vs further selling
tension_points.bull_case: UBS expects SPX could set a low on Monday. Three capitulation signals have triggered, Risk Control and CTA selling should become very small after Monday, and net long exposure is already very low with short-squeeze risk high. VIX fell 80% of the time and SPX rose 80% of the time over 1M in past cases.
tension_points.bear_case: Risk Control still needs to sell $200-270bn over the next two days. Retail margin-call selling is expected, close CTA sell triggers remain at ES1 7348.4 and RTY1 2723.4, and the VIX/SPX hi-low ratio test is not met.
tension_points.what_invalidates: SPX falling about 3% on the next session would mean roughly $45bn more Risk Control selling, and a break of the 7348.4 ES1 CTA trigger would add sell pressure. The VIX/SPX hi-low signal would need SPX below about -9.5% from peak.

theme_stances.key_argument: Systematic and hedge-fund unwind pressure should fade after Monday, so SPX could establish a low then.
